cues.en: So the talk that I was asked tonight, actually I was totally free to decide on the theme, and I decided to talk on something which is, I believe, dramatically not assessed or not studied, which is the link between economics and physics.
cues.zh: 今晚的演讲主题完全由我自定，我决定聊一个我认为极度缺乏研究和评估的话题，那就是经济学与物理学之间的联系。

cues.en: And the conclusion to which I am going to draw you in a way is that when you put physics into economics, you come up with results that are not very easy to sell in an election. If you look, actually, at the conventional speech on the question that is raised here, the answer is yes.
cues.zh: 而我想带大家得出的结论是：一旦把物理学引入经济学，得出的结果在竞选时可很难卖得出去。但如果你看关于这个问题的传统说辞，答案却总是肯定的。

cues.en: Yes, you can have everything at the same time. Actually, a body which is called the United Nations, which is supposed to be a serious one, or at least a place where a large number of people should agree on serious things. They tell you that we have sustainable development goals, 17 to be precise. And so these sustainable development goals should be achieved all at the same time. And actually, if you pile them one on top of the other, it's close to Alice in Wonderland.
cues.zh: 是的，你能全都要。比如联合国这样一个理应严肃的机构——至少是个大家商讨严肃议题的地方——他们告诉你，我们有 17 项可持续发展目标，而且必须同时实现；但如果把它们堆在一起看，简直就像《爱丽丝梦游仙境》一样魔幻。

cues.en: You are going to satisfy economists. You are going to satisfy doctors. You are going to satisfy people that teach something. You are going to satisfy feminists. You are going to satisfy people that drink water, which is quite a great number of people. You're going to satisfy mayors. You're going to satisfy industrials. You're going to satisfy the consumers. Do not forget the consumers. Of course, you're going to satisfy people that care about the environment.
cues.zh: 你要让经济学家满意、让医生满意、让教师满意、让女权主义者满意，让喝水的人满意（这可是绝大多数人），让市长满意、让工业界满意，还要让消费者满意——别忘了消费者，当然还要让环保人士满意。

cues.en: OK, so everybody's going to be satisfied. I mean, this or any pre-electoral speech is about the same. Vote for me, and I'm going to bring you happiness. Whoever you are, whatever you go is. The short answer is no, so we can all go out and have a drink. I'm trying to give you a longer answer during the time slot that I was allowed. And to give you the longer answer, I'm going to go through something which is called energy. You probably know.
cues.zh: 行，所有人都满意。这和任何竞选演讲没两样：“选我，我就能带给你幸福，不论你是谁，不论你的目标是什么。”简短的回答是“不可能”，所以咱们直接散伙去喝一杯也行。不过在给定的时间里，我会尝试给出一个更详尽的回答，而这绕不开一个叫作“能源”的东西，大家大概知道……

cues.en: that we have a minister in France in charge of energy matters. Actually, it's been a very long time that we have had in France somebody in charge of energy matters. I'm ready to bet with about anybody in the room that if I ask to the minister in charge what is energy exactly, I will get anything but the right answer. So if anybody is ready to bet, I take all the bets when leaving the room.
cues.zh: ……在法国，我们设有专门主管能源事务的部长。事实上法国很早以前就设立了这个职位。我敢跟在座的各位打赌，如果我去问那位主管部长“能源到底是什么”，他给出的回答绝对不可能是对的。如果有谁想打赌，散场离开时我随时奉陪。

cues.en: Because when you ask the question to the general population, and the general population and the minister in charge actually basically think the same way, that's how democracy works, you will get this answer. Energy is a bill.
cues.zh: 因为如果你去问普通大众——大众和主管部长的想法基本如出一辙，民主就是这么运作的——你会得到这样的回答：“能源就是账单。”

cues.en: And at least something you pay, something you purchase, actually. The first thing you're going to think about is your electricity bill, because that's the bill that you receive. Everybody receives an electricity bill, basically, except for tramps that live in the street. The second thing that you might think of, because a number of people have a central heating that operates with gas, is a gas bill. Some very clever people might think of the gasoline that they buy at the pump.
cues.zh: 至少是你花钱支付、实际购买的东西。你首先会想到的就是电费单，因为那是你会收到的账单。基本上每个人都会收到电费单，除非是露宿街头的流浪汉。你可能想到的第二件事是燃气费，因为很多人家里用的是天然气集中供暖。更聪明一点的人可能会想到去加油站加的汽油。

cues.en: But that's it. I mean, energy is a bill. Well, it happens that if you answer energy is a bill, you have just allied yourself with the economist and it's the wrong answer. It's the wrong answer because if you look at the size of the bill compared to all what we spend, it's a small bill, a very small bill. This curve gives you the fraction of the spendings that are devoted to buying energy. What it tells is that except during oil shocks,
cues.zh: 但也就仅此而已了。我的意思是，在大家眼里能源就是一张账单。好吧，如果你认为能源只是一张账单，那你恰恰站到了经济学家的阵营，而这是个错误的答案。之所以错，是因为如果你看看这笔账单在我们所有支出中的占比，它其实微不足道，比例非常小。这条曲线展示了用于购买能源的支出占总开支的比例。它表明，除了在石油危机期间，

cues.en: What the world spends on average to buy oil gas and coal and I will know I do not have a curve today But I remind you that 65% of the electricity produced on earth comes from coal and gas so first you buy oil and gas Coal and gas sorry is a couple percent of our revenues so on average in the world You I we spent a couple percent of our revenues on energy
cues.zh: 全世界平均花在购买石油、天然气和煤炭上的开销——我今天手头没有具体的曲线，但我提醒大家，全球65%的电力来自煤炭和天然气，所以首先你购买石油和天然气……抱歉，是煤炭和天然气——只占我们收入的百分之几。因此按全球平均来看，你、我，大家花在能源上的钱只占收入的百分之几。

cues.en: It's negligible. In France, you spent one third of your revenue on housing. That's a serious matter. Then you spend 10% of your revenue on food. It's almost a serious matter. Used to be about three or four times this. You spend a couple percent of your revenues on phoning to a friend saying that you're going to be late, which is about the same amount of money that you spent on energy. So energy is negligible in our spendings.
cues.zh: 这是微不足道的。在法国，三分之一的收入要花在住房上，这可是件大事。然后你把10%的收入花在食物上，这也很重要，以前甚至比这还要高三到四倍。你花百分之几的收入给朋友打电话说你要迟到了，这跟你在能源上花的钱差不多。所以，能源在我们的日常开销中完全微不足道。

cues.en: And because it is negligible, that is, it's a couple percent of our spendings, when you talk to Homo economicus, the reflex that he will have is saying, okay, if it's a couple percent of my spendings, I'm going to deal with the topic a couple percent of my time, and that's it. I'm done with it. Now I can deal with serious things, geopolitics, pension funds, whatever, not energy. Okay, so energy, I take a minister for that, give him instructions, and sorry to say it in French, as Dougal said,
cues.zh: 正因为它微不足道，只占支出的百分之几，当你和“经济人”交流时，他的本能反应就是：行吧，既然它只占我开销的百分之几，那我就花百分之几的时间来处理这个问题，到此为止。完事了。现在我可以去处理真正严肃的大事了，比如地缘政治、养老基金等等，反正不是能源。能源问题嘛，我找个部长来管，给他交代几句，借用法语里戴高乐的名言来说就是：

cues.en: l'attendant suivre. No big deal. Well, thinking like this is about as relevant as if you said my brain is 2% of my weight. So I can take care of my brain 2% of the time. And the rest of the time, it's of no use taking care of my brain. I can do whatever I want with my brain. Or I can devote to somebody
cues.zh: “后勤自会跟上”。没什么大不了的。但是，这么想的合理程度，就相当于你在说：我的大脑只占体重的2%，所以我只要花2%的时间去管我的脑子就行了。剩下的时间，根本没必要管大脑，拿它做什么都行。或者我可以委托一个人……

cues.en: to take care of all the brains, and I'm going to give him 2% of whatever, and I can independently look at the rest with other people. Of course, it doesn't work because our body is a coupled system, and if I remove half of your brain, I just do not diminish your weight by 1%, and therefore you power by 1%. I just kill you.
cues.zh: 去照管所有的大脑，我给他2%的资源，然后我再跟其他人各管各的去顾身体的其他部分。这显然行不通，因为我们的身体是一个紧密耦合的系统。如果我切掉你半个脑子，可不仅仅是让你的体重减少1%、从而让你的力量减弱1%。我这是直接要了你的命。

cues.en: What I'm going to explain is that it's exactly the same thing for energy. Actually, we just don't care about how much it costs. It's just not the point. We just don't care. Now, let's suppose that we still ask the question. There is a second very common answer, which is, when you hear energy, you think savings. Energy is something we must save. Again, it's a wrong answer.
cues.zh: 我要解释的是，能源也是完全一样的道理。实际上，我们根本不在乎它要花多少钱。这根本不是重点。我们就是不在乎。现在，假设我们还是要问这个问题。还有第二种非常普遍的回答，那就是：一听到能源，你就会想到节约。能源是我们必须节约的东西。同样，这也是个错误的回答。

cues.en: If you are all in this room with the time to listen to me instead of growing potatoes, it's precisely because for the last two centuries we haven't saved energy. It's precisely because of this. If during the last two centuries we had saved energy, there would be 500 million peasants on Earth. No students here. Or a handful. Because it's because of the productive system, the tremendously productive system that we have set up with machines.
cues.zh: 如果你们大家能坐在这间屋子里，有时间听我讲，而不是去种土豆，正是因为过去两个世纪我们没有节约能源。恰恰就是这个原因。如果在过去两个世纪里我们一直在节约能源，地球上就会有5亿农民。这里也不会有学生，或者寥寥无几。因为正是靠着这套生产体系，这套我们用机器建立起来的高效生产体系，

cues.en: that we have enough time to do everything else than growing potatoes. Second wrong answer. A large number of people just have no idea. It's okay with them, because there is a minister in charge, okay? And if you ask a poet, well, the poet is going to give you what is the closest to the good answer, which is energy is something you're full of a morning that you're in great shape. Well, actually, that's the good answer. Because as you probably know in this room,
cues.zh: 我们才有足够的时间去做种土豆以外的所有事情。第二个错误答案。很大一部分人对此一无所知。但他们觉得无所谓，反正有部长管着，对吧？如果你去问一个诗人，诗人会给出最接近正确答案的回答，那就是：能量就是你在状态极佳的早晨浑身充满的东西。其实，这反而是个好答案。因为在座各位可能都知道，

cues.en: Energy is by definition in physics what quantifies change. So if you are packed up with energy, you are packed up with the ability to change your environment and that is you are packed up with the ability to master your destiny. So energy is by definition what allows you to change the environment by definition. For that only you need a converter, of course. You cannot use energy in a raw way. So energy is something that...
cues.zh: 在物理学中，能量的定义就是量化变化的物理量。所以如果你充满能量，你就具备了改变环境的能力，也就是说，你具备了掌控自己命运的能力。因此，根据定义，能量就是让你能够改变环境的东西。当然，要做到这一点，你需要一个转换器。你无法直接使用原始形态的能量。所以能量就是……

cues.en: enables you to master your environment. And because of the law of conservation that you probably know better than I do, all we can do regarding energy is actually not produce or producing energy. It is extracting energy from the environment, or it is already there, and use it into a converter to get something that we deem useful. That's all we can do with energy.
cues.zh: 能让你掌控环境的东西。而且由于大家可能比我更清楚的能量守恒定律，关于能量，我们其实根本无法“生产”或“创造”它。我们所能做的，不过是从环境中提取早已存在的能量，再通过转换器将其转化为我们认为有用的形态。这就是我们对能量所能做的一切。

cues.en: The energy that we get from the environment, we often call it primary energy. So when you read primary energy somewhere, it's the energy that already exists in the environment, namely things that burn, oil, gas, coal, wood, waterfalls, wind that blows, etc. That's primary energy. Of course, part of the primary energy we find into the environment is chemical energy in the form of edible products.
cues.zh: 我们从环境中获取的能量，通常被称为一次能源。所以当你在哪里看到“一次能源”时，指的就是自然界中原本就存在的能量，也就是能燃烧的东西、石油、天然气、煤炭、木材、瀑布水流、刮起的风等等。这就是一次能源。当然，我们在环境中发现的一部分一次能源，是以食物形式存在的化学能。

cues.en: That's the first energy that humanity has used, and it has used it with the only converter that was available at the time that is our own body. So we take that energy from the environment, say kilo mammoth, we eat it, and that gives us enough energy to remain at 37 degrees Celsius, and move around so that we can hunt other mammoths, okay? So that's the first converter that we have at hand. But today, we have, thanks to Carnot, Papa, and others,
cues.zh: 那是人类使用的第一种能量，而当时唯一可用的转换器，就是我们自己的身体。我们从环境中获取这种能量，比如吃下一公斤猛犸象肉，这能提供足够的能量让我们维持37摄氏度的体温、四处活动，从而去捕猎下一头猛犸象，对吧？这就是我们手头的第一个转换器。但如今，多亏了 Carnot、Papa 等人，

cues.en: discovered another number of converters that we can use and that we can use with other forms of energy than edible products. Those are the machines that surround us today, everywhere, all the time. These machines have enabled us to convert other forms of energy because when somebody says that you consume energy, actually that's false. You do not drink oil and you do not breathe gas and you do not eat coal.
cues.zh: 我们发现了大量其他的转换器，能够利用食物之外的其他能量形式。这些转换器就是如今随时随地围绕着我们的机器。这些机器让我们得以转换其他形式的能量，因为如果有人说你在消耗能源，其实这并不准确。你又不会喝石油、呼吸天然气，也不会去吃煤炭。

cues.en: So you do not consume energy. Actually what you really do when somebody says that you consume energy is that you use a machine that converts the energy. That's what you do. So using more and more energy you must remove that expression from your heads and think using more and more machines. That's what it means to say we are using more and more energy. It means we are using more and more machines that have a greater and greater ability
cues.zh: 所以你其实并不消耗能量。实际上，当有人说你在消耗能量时，你真正做的是使用一台机器去转换能量。这就是你所做的事。因此，“使用越来越多的能量”这种说法，大家必须从脑海中抹掉，应该想成是“使用越来越多的机器”。说我们在消耗越来越多的能量，意思就是我们在使用越来越多的机器，它们拥有越来越强大的能力，

cues.en: to create physical flows into the environment. That's what we really do when we consume more and more energy. The amount of energy that we are now able to get through machines is tremendously more important than what our own body is able to provide. My father, among his accomplishments, was also modest as I am, mountaineer. So he was once in a while in the mountains.
cues.zh: 向自然环境中输出物理通量。这就是我们消耗越来越多能量时真正在做的事。如今我们能借助机器获取的能量规模，远远超过我们肉体自身所能提供的上限。我父亲除了其他成就之外，也和我一样谦逊，他是一名登山爱好者。所以他过去偶尔会去登山。

cues.en: You can also imagine climbing up the Eiffel Tower as well. So let's assume, for example, that every morning before breakfast, in order to feel in great shape, just as I said before, you climb up, let's say, 6.5 times the Eiffel Tower on foot, not with the lift. The advantage, of course, is that you have less Japanese tourists when you climb up. If you do this...
cues.zh: 你也可以想象去爬埃菲尔铁塔。比方说我们假设，每天早饭前为了让自己精力充沛，就像我刚才说的，你徒步爬上埃菲尔铁塔6.5次，不坐电梯。好处当然是，你爬的时候日本游客会少很多。如果你真这么做……

cues.en: And if you weight 80 kilograms plus 10 of your backpack, that's only because the calculation is simple. Of course, what I use is the very basic formula, which is E equals mgh. It's as simple as this. You come up with the conclusion that all that your body can yield in a great effort that lasts for one day is a ridiculous half kilowatt hour. If you use your legs, you can use your arms. That's convenient. But if you use your legs,
cues.zh: 再加上你体重80公斤，背包10公斤——这么设只是为了好算。当然，我用的是最基础的公式，也就是 E 等于 mgh。就是这么简单。你会得出结论：你拼尽全力折腾一整天，身体所能输出的能量少得可怜，只有区区半度电。如果你用腿，当然你也可以用手臂，这很方便。但如果你用双腿，

cues.en: to climb up 2,000 meters, all you have provided in the form of mechanical energy is a ridiculous half kilowatt hour. Fully ridiculous. If you do this one day out of two, or every day you climb up 1,000 meters, at the end of the year, you're able to provide 100 kilowatt hours of mechanical energy. That's the order of magnitude of the mechanical energy that the human body is able to provide over a year.
cues.zh: 向上攀爬2000米，你以机械能形式输出的全部能量，就只有可怜的半度电。简直可笑至极。如果你隔天爬一次，或者每天爬1000米，一年下来，你能提供的机械能也就100度电。这就是人体一年所能输出的机械能数量级。

cues.en: If instead of using your legs, you use your arms to shovel up earth, same thing, E equals NGH. You come up with the conclusion that you are 10 times more ridiculous because with this kind of effort, you will provide 0.05 kilowatt hour over a year of mechanical energy. Totally ridiculous. Totally ridiculous. In one single liter of gasoline, one single liter of gasoline,
cues.zh: 如果你不用腿，而是用手臂去铲土，也是一样的，E 等于 mgh。你会发现结果还要可笑十倍，因为照这样干，你一年输出的机械能只有0.05度电。极其可笑，荒谬透顶。而仅仅一升汽油，仅仅一升汽油，

cues.en: And I remind that in France, we use roughly 1,000 liters of gasoline per capita and per year, despite the fact that we're supposed to be all nuclear. So one single liter of gasoline encloses 10 kilowatt-hour of thermal energy.
cues.zh: 顺便提一句，在法国，尽管大家以为我们全是核电，但人均每年依然要消耗大约1000升汽油。而仅仅一升汽油，就蕴含着10度电的热能。

cues.en: And if you put this into a machine, of course you have the counter yield, you are going to get out of this machine two to four kilowatt hours of mechanical energy, which means that in a single liter of gasoline, you've got the same ability to transform the environment that you have in 10 to 100 days of hard human labor. That's what machines mean for us. Now, if you convert this into money, it means that if you take the person
cues.zh: 如果你把这些能量输入机器，当然会有转换效率的折损，但你依然能从这台机器中获取两到四千瓦时的机械能，这意味着仅仅一升汽油，其改造自然环境的能力，就相当于人类进行 10 到 100 天繁重的体力劳动。这就是机器对我们的意义。现在，如果把它折算成金钱，意味着如果你雇佣一个人……

cues.en: that changes the environment. If you hire that person at the minimum wage, the human kilowatt hour is going to cost you anything between a couple hundred and a couple thousand euros when the machine is going to provide the same service for, I do not count the cost of the machine, for a marginal cost of 10 cents. So going from man to machine is a way to divide by a factor of several thousand
cues.zh: ……来改造自然。如果你按最低工资雇佣这个人，人工提供一千瓦时的成本将在几百到几千欧元之间，而机器提供同样的服务——这里还不算机器本身的购置成本——边际成本只要 10 欧分。因此，从人力转向机器，能把成本降低几千倍……

cues.en: to several hundred, depending on the efficiency, the cost of unitary transformation, physical transformation of the environment, namely building one square meter of housing, that's physical, transporting one ton of goods, that's physical, manufacturing one chair, that's physical, growing one carrot. This is why your purchasing power has increased. This is why you can have negotiation on your wages and believe you're going to win.
cues.zh: ……到数百倍，具体取决于转换效率；也就是大幅降低了对环境进行单次物理改造的成本：比如建一平米房屋，这是物理改造；运输一吨货物，这是物理改造；造一把椅子，这是物理改造；种一根胡萝卜也是。这就是为什么你的购买力提升了。这也是为什么你能去争取加薪，并且坚信自己能谈成。

cues.en: It's not because your boss is somebody fabulous. It's just because we have had this two century increase in productivity due to this. So the only reason why the budget of research has increased is there. And the reason why it's going to decrease from now is there also we're going to see afterwards. It's physical. It's physical. Now let's suppose that we take a slave. The definition of a slave...

cues.zh: 外生要素，即资本和劳动，而 GDP 是由这两个要素决定的内生变量。但正如我开头所说，能源被当成一种商品，是有了 GDP 之后才去购买的产品，所以能源又是 GDP 的内生变量。基于这种逻辑，首先得有足够能干活的人和足够的人力资本。

cues.zh: 然后你说，好，我们还有动物。于是我把动物加起来，这相当于若干工人。我得出结论：你能投入农业的机械动力——因为当时有生物奴隶，也就是动物——相当于我们人力身体总量的四倍。

cues.en: And he says, we can do the same thing for industry. So I can consider watermills and windmills, et cetera, as equivalent of human bodies. And that also gives me the productive force of not only the population, but the population and the machines that we were able to master at the time. So Charles Dupin correctly understands at the time that production is not done by men. Production is done by men and machines. And when machines represent
cues.zh: 他说，工业也可以这样做。所以我可以把水磨、风磨等看作人力身体的当量。这样我得到的不只是人口的生产力，而是人口加上当时我们能掌握的机器的生产力。所以 Charles Dupin 当时正确理解到，生产不是由人完成的。生产是由人和机器完成的。而当机器代表

cues.en: Much more than men, actually, the first order approximation is not I take population and capital, but I take machines and something else. And that's exactly the way to think. Actually, if you have products in the supermarket, you need the raw materials to produce the product, because if you have atoms of copper into something you buy, you have to find the atom of copper somewhere in the environment. cues.zh: 远多于人时，实际上，一阶近似不是取人口和资本，而是取机器和其他东西。这才是正确的思考方式。实际上，超市里的产品需要原材料来生产，因为你买的某个东西里若有铜原子，你就得在环境某处找到那个铜原子。你不会因为银行里有信用额度就创造出一个铜原子。

cues.en: It doesn't work. So all you can do is find it into the environment. And same thing, actually, for all the elements of the table of Mendeleev. So if nature had not created for us and for free the 92 elements of the table of Mendeleev, we wouldn't have any cent of GDP. But that's free. So we need resources to transform, and we need the ability to transform these resources, namely
cues.zh: 这行不通。所以你能做的只是到环境中找到它。实际上，Mendeleev 元素周期表里的所有元素都是如此。如果大自然没有为我们免费创造 Mendeleev 元素周期表的 92 种元素，我们连一分钱 GDP 都不会有。但那是免费的。所以我们需要可转化的资源，也需要转化这些资源的能力，也就是

cues.en: human beings at the beginning and now machines and the food of their own, that is energy, which accounts for 200 if humanity accounts for one. And there you see that the bottleneck which is going to have the importance of the first order is not do we have enough men, but do we have enough energy? That's the true bottleneck. It's the only one to look at. Capital in this system is only an internal loop.
cues.zh: 起初是人类，现在是机器以及机器自己的食物，也就是能源；如果人类算 1，能源就算 200。于是你看到，具有一阶重要性的瓶颈不是我们有没有足够的人，而是我们有没有足够的能源？这才是真正的瓶颈。这是唯一需要看的。这个系统里的资本只是一个内部循环。

cues.en: Because you produce a building exactly the way you produce a pair of glasses, you take resources into the environment, transform it with machines and men into something else which we deem more valuable. It's exactly the same physical process. The only difference is that consumer goods is something that are supposed to be destroyed when you use them, or destroyed pretty fast, whereas capital goods is something that is not destroyed when you use it. But that's the difference.
cues.zh: 建造一栋大楼和制造一副眼镜的方式完全一样：都是从自然界获取资源，再通过机器和人力将其转化为我们认为更有价值的东西。这完全是相同的物理过程。唯一的区别在于，消费品在使用时会被消耗掉，或者很快消耗掉；而资本品在使用时则不会被消耗。区别仅此而已。

cues.en: Now if in this flow chart You have a bottleneck on energy for whatever reason you might lack Energy or you might decide that you are going to compress the energy supply in the sake of climate Doesn't make any difference there. You are going to compress the mechanical Input of machines and then you are going to contract The outgoing flow that is production less energy less consumer goods
cues.zh: 现在，如果这个流程图中能源环节出现了瓶颈——不论是因为能源短缺，还是为了应对气候变化而主动压缩能源供应，结果都一样。机器的机械输入被压缩，最终的产出流就会收缩，也就是生产受阻：能源越少，产出的消费品就越少。

cues.en: We are going to see that in a minute. If you have less resources, it works the same way. It works the same way. And this is the reason why, when you look at the world as a whole, the best macroeconomic model that I have found so far is a straight line. A straight line. On the horizontal axis, you have energy, which is actually the number of machines that we use. And on the vertical axis,
cues.zh: 我们马上就会看到这一点。如果资源变少，逻辑也是完全一样的。完全一样。这就是为什么纵观全球，我目前发现的最好的宏观经济模型居然是一条直线。一条直线。横轴是能源，它实际上代表着我们使用的机器数量。而在纵轴上，

cues.en: You have the economic counterpart of the physical flows that we have created with these machines, namely added values piled up on top of the others, that is the GDP. So this is the logical conclusion of having production devoted to machines that are 200 times more powerful than humanity. You should expect this graph to look like this.
cues.zh: 则是这些机器创造的物理流所对应的经济价值，即层层累加的附加值，也就是 GDP。因此，当生产依赖于比人类强大 200 倍的机器时，这就是必然的逻辑推论。图表本就该是这个样子。

cues.en: And it is a matter of amount. It is not a matter of price. And I've got a second conclusion that might hurt a little economist in this room if there are some. There is absolutely no such thing as an elasticity between price and volume. You know, a number of people say, OK, you have a product. If you have more of that product, it costs less. And if you have less of that product, it costs more. Wrong answer. This chart is a plot.
cues.zh: 关键在于总量，而不是价格。我的第二个结论可能会让在场的某些经济学家有点难受：价格和供给量之间根本不存在所谓的弹性。很多人说：一种产品如果变多了，价格就会下降；变少了，价格就会上涨。大错特错。这张图绘制的是……

cues.en: of the amount of oil which is offered on the world market and the price of the barrel of oil. And the dots here begin in 1921. I removed the dots before because otherwise they would have occupied too much space here. And it goes to 2015, but it doesn't make much difference if I had put 2016. If you had had an elasticity, dots should be organized this way. More oil, cheaper, less oil, costier.
cues.zh: 全球市场供应的石油总量与每桶石油价格的关系。图中的数据点始于 1921 年，我去掉了更早的数据，否则这里就挤不下了。数据一直持续到 2015 年，不过就算算上 2016 年也没什么差别。如果真有价格弹性，这些点应该这样排列：石油越多越便宜，石油越少越贵。

cues.en: Very simple. What you look at here is anything but that. Actually, it's not objective to begin with. You give me a price, I can't give you a volume. Actually, if you look at this graph, you can say that the first order approximation is that you have two orthogonal inelastic regimes. One regime in which the volume can do anything it wants and the price remains constant. Then another regime.
cues.zh: 非常简单。但眼前的图表完全不是这样。事实上，连基本的对应关系都没有：你给我一个价格，我根本给不出对应的供给量。从图上看，一阶近似其实是两个相互正交的无弹性区间：在其中一个区间里，供给量无论怎么变化，价格都保持恒定；而在另一个区间里……

cues.en: which is the exact opposite in a way, where the price does anything and the volume remains about constant. Then again, a regime in which the price wobbles a little around fixed value when the volume is changing a lot. Then again, et cetera. So there is absolutely no link between the nominal price and the volume. So anybody who is using, and I know economists that do use, an elasticity, a long-term elasticity,
cues.zh: 某种程度上正好相反，价格随便怎么变，而产量基本保持不变。接着又是另一种状态，价格在固定值附近轻微波动，而产量剧烈变化。然后又是这样，等等。所以名义价格与产量之间根本没有任何关联。因此，任何人如果使用——我知道确实有经济学家在用——弹性，也就是长期弹性，

cues.en: because you have a short-term elasticity. But the long-term elasticity between prices and volumes regarding energy or actually any commodity in a model is bound to give you a result which is false, because there is no such relationship. Now, once I've said this, again, the question is, what happens if we go back to the original question? Now, as you have understood, production is not a matter of men being helped by machines. It's a matter of machines being helped by men.
cues.zh: 因为短期弹性确实存在。但在模型中，能源或其实任何大宗商品的价格与产量之间的长期弹性，必然会得出错误的结果，因为根本不存在这种关系。说了这么多，问题依然是，如果我们回到最初的问题会怎样？现在你们明白了，生产并不是人借助机器，而是机器借助人。

cues.en: The driver of the tractor is only there to guide the tractor. It's not the driver of the tractor which is plowing the earth. It's the tractor. So if you can remove the driver and replace it by software, you have the same crop. If you remove the tractor and keep the driver, you do not have the same crop. So it's the machine which is producing. The man is just there to give orders.
cues.zh: 拖拉机司机只是在那里给拖拉机带路。在耕地的并不是司机，而是拖拉机。所以如果把司机拿掉换成软件，收成还是一样。要是去掉拖拉机只留司机，收成可就完全不同了。所以进行生产的是机器，人只是在那里发号施令。

cues.en: And that's true for tractors because the power of a tractor is 600 times the power of a pair of legs. The power of a machine of public works is a thousand times, order of magnitude, the power of the pair of arms that it replaces. So same thing. If you keep the machine and put the software in it, you get the same production. If you remove the machine and keep the driver, you do not really get the same production. It's because of machines like this.
cues.zh: 拖拉机是这样，因为一台拖拉机的功率是双腿力量的 600 倍。工程机械的功率数量级，是它所替代的双臂力量的 1000 倍。所以同理，保留机器并植入软件，你能得到相同的产出；如果去掉机器只留司机，你根本不可能得到相同的产出。这正是因为这类机器的存在。

cues.en: Plus other machines That I'm going to show for example this one Plus the salmon factories again machines plus the steel meals again machine cetera that today We're able to build a tower in la defense in one year When it took one century to build Notre Dame with muscles cheap housing is machines No machines, no cheap housing very simple. So the whole argument is a child of energy

And if you look at the steel mill, precisely, you would require to replace a single steel mill, which can be operated by a single person.

You hammer steel all day just to replace one steel mill if we have no energy. So these machines, they are tremendous. Now, what happens if we have less machines? Are we going to replace them by men? So if you have less energy, someone can think that we are going to replace machines by men.
cues.zh: 你就得把法兰西岛的所有居民都叫来，人手发一把锤子，让他们整天打铁。所以你们也不用在这里学物理了，如果没了能源，光是替代一座钢铁厂就得整天去打铁。所以这些机器极其强大。那么，如果我们的机器变少了会怎样？我们要用人力去替代它们吗？因此，当能源变少时，有人可能会认为我们可以用人来替代机器。

cues.en: And that's a good thing for employment. Unfortunately, that's a wrong answer. If you have a machine plus the food of its own, plus the driver of the machine, you have the equivalent, take a tractor, of 600 men. Now let's suppose that you contract the energy supply. That means that you are going to contract the amount of machines that can work. And you say, OK, it's a good thing. I'm going to replace, namely in this example,
cues.zh: 这对就业是好事。可惜，这个答案是错的。一台机器，加上它自身所需的燃料，再加上操作机器的司机，相当于——以拖拉机为例——600个人。现在假设你缩减能源供应。这意味着你能运转的机器数量会减少。你说，好啊，这是好事。我要替换掉，也就是在这个例子里，

cues.en: half of the machine I do not have anymore by 300 men. That would be correct if paying a man was one on 300 times paying a machine. Then you have an economic equivalent, and you say, OK, I remove the machine, replace it by 300 men, cost me exactly the same. But it happens that it's not the case. The machine costs you a couple men. So what happens if you have
cues.zh: 用300个人替换掉我不再拥有的一半机器。如果雇一个人的成本是一台机器的三百分之一，那这才成立。这样你才有经济等价，你说，好，我撤掉机器，用300个人替代，成本完全一样。但事实并非如此。一台机器的成本只相当于几个人。那么，如果你有

cues.en: less machines is that first you're going to have less GDP because you cannot replace the machine by a productive force, which costs you the same thing. And as the man is there only to drive the machine, you have less jobs. So with the tremendous difference between the productivity of a machine and the productivity of men, what we do today if we contract the energy supply in the first order is that we are going to contract at the same time the GDP and the jobs.
cues.zh: 更少的机器，首先你的GDP会更低，因为你无法用成本相同的生产力来替代机器。而且人只是在那里操作机器，所以工作岗位也会减少。因此，机器生产率与人的生产率之间存在巨大差异，我们今天如果首先缩减能源供应，就会同时缩减GDP和就业。

cues.en: I do not only say that, I prove it. This is the energy supply of Spain. The energy supply of Spain peaked in 2007. Who knew it? No one. It's not in the paper. Putting in service a new windmill is in the paper every day. This is not in the paper. This is much more dramatic for the future of Europe than erecting a new windmill. Much more dramatic, I can tell you.
cues.zh: 我不只是说说，我要证明它。这是西班牙的能源供应。西班牙的能源供应在2007年达到峰值。谁知道？没人知道。报纸上没报道。启用一台新风力发电机天天上报纸。这件事却没上报纸。这对欧洲的未来，比竖起一台新风力发电机要严重得多。我可以告诉你，严重得多。

cues.en: So the energy supply peaked. Why did it peak? Because the energy supply of Spain at the time was mostly oil. And the supply of conventional oil, that is all oil which is not shale oil and tar sands in the world, peaked in 2006. It's not in the paper either. But it's real. So it peaked. So because it peaked, the energy supply coming from oil decreased. And as it was the dominant share,
cues.zh: 所以能源供应达峰了。为什么达峰？因为当时西班牙的能源供应主要来自石油。而常规石油——也就是全球所有非页岩油和油砂的石油——的供应在2006年达峰。这也没上报纸。但它是真的。所以它见顶了。正因为见顶，来自石油的能源供应减少了。而由于它占主导份额，

cues.en: of the energy supply of Spain, the energy supply of Spain decreased. Now look at the number of people that work in Spain compared to the population. That's something which should be used instead of the unemployment rate because the unemployment rate is the fraction of people that wish a job that do not work. But it is not something relevant because you have to ask the people whether they wish a job or not. This curve here, it's the employment to population ratio which is
cues.zh: 也就是西班牙能源供应中的主导份额，因此西班牙能源供应下降了。现在看看西班牙工作人数与人口之比。这个指标应该用来取代失业率，因为失业率是想工作却没工作的人所占比例。但它并不相关，因为你得问人们想不想要工作。这里这条曲线，是就业人口比，也就是

cues.en: the fraction of the population aged of 15 or plus, that does work. It's a physical indicator. You do not need to ask the people whether they want a job or not. Because if people don't want a job, because they said that they are tired of looking for a job, or because they said that now they have some kind of training that they believe will provide them a job later on, even if it's not true, et cetera, you remove them from the unemployment statistics. So there is a very simple way to decrease the rate of unemployment.
cues.zh: 15岁及以上人口中实际工作的人所占比例。这是个客观指标。你不需要问人们想不想要工作。因为如果人们不想要工作——比如他们说厌倦找工作了，或者他们说现在参加了某种培训，相信以后能给自己带来工作，即使这并不属实，等等——你就把他们从失业统计中剔除了。所以，降低失业率有一个非常简单的办法。

cues.en: It's to make so that people do not want the job anymore. Do not laugh. About half of the unemployment in the US was sold this way. Just this way. So this is the employment to population ratio in Spain. And what you can see is that the fraction of the population that is able to have a job in Spain is far from having regained the level of 2007. Far from having regained that. So if you look at the dynamics, OK, growth is back.
cues.zh: 就是让大家不再想找工作了。别笑，美国大概有一半的失业问题就是这么解决的。就是这么回事。这是西班牙的就业人口比例。大家可以看到，西班牙能够拥有工作的人口比例，远未恢复到 2007 年的水平。差得远呢。如果看发展态势，好吧，增长确实回来了。

GDP decreases.

cues.zh: 是为了数桌子、椅子、汽车之类的东西。所以实际上，正如 Marcel Bueto 所说，钱是我们发明出来比较一堆本来不可比较之物的东西。所以基本上，我们给所有这些事物赋予价值，把它们堆在一起，这就是 GDP。它衡量的就是这个，仅此而已，不多不少。而如果你正确计入通胀——今天对普通商品大致会做，对资产则完全没做，

cues.zh: 因为过去 10 年 GDP 增长的大部分是资产通胀。这部分并没有在 GDP 计算中被扣除。但如果你正确扣除通胀，GDP 基本上反映的就是人们能买到的东西数量。所以如果 GDP 更少，他们能买的东西就更少。现在真正的问题是：你该如何组织社会，才能在这种情况下仍然保持相当和平的局面？

Because the boundaries are not the same. The energy consumption is something which is domestic.
cues.zh: 晚上好。您给我们展示了GDP与能源消耗之间呈线性关系的不同曲线。但比如丹麦这样的国家，自70年代以来GDP翻了一番，能源消耗却没有增加。那您如何在模型中解释这一点？因为边界并不相同。能源消耗是国内的事情。

cues.en: The GDP takes into account physical flows that happen outside Denmark. cues.zh: GDP会把发生在丹麦之外的实物流动纳入计算。当MERSC运营一艘从巴西开往比如南非的船时，运营这艘船带来的部分收入记在丹麦。但让这笔收入得以存在的能源消耗发生在丹麦之外。所以当你有一个小国家——抱歉说丹麦是小国——但当你有一个小国家时，

cues.en: which is very open to international trade, which is the case for Denmark. And by the way, also the case for Sweden, another country that I know pretty well. cues.zh: 它非常开放于国际贸易，丹麦就是如此。顺便说，瑞典也是如此，另一个我很熟悉的国家。就其经济框架而言，你可以有——瑞士也完全一样——资金流入这个国家，但能源流向别处。这就是为什么有因果到结果的关系，因为它是因到果。先有能源，后有GDP。

cues.en: If you have more energy, you can transform more things and create more GDP. If you have more GDP, it means that you have more things. But if you look at, if you perform things that look like grandeur or causality tests,
cues.zh: 如果你有更多能源，你就能转化更多东西，创造更多GDP。如果你有更多GDP，意味着你有更多东西。而在这些东西中，你可以有投资，让你更快地开采剩余能源。所以这是一个耦合系统。但如果你看，如果你做类似Granger或因果性检验的东西，
